Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 01-Jan-2026 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - JANUARY 2026  
  Software Engineering [NPT_4123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                 Apply the principles of abstraction and decomposition to explain how software engineers manage          (5)  
  cognitive limitations while designing and maintaining complex software systems. Briefly describe  
  A)            how each principle simplifies understanding and problem-solving, and draw a schematic diagram  
  that represents hierarchical abstraction levels and modular decomposition in a generic software  
  system.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Analyze the concept of computer systems engineering and compare it with software engineering.           (5)  
  Identify and discuss examples of product development projects where systems engineering would  
  be most appropriately applied.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                 Apply your understanding of the Evolutionary Development model to explain how it supports               (5)  
  accommodating changing user requirements during software development. Illustrate your  
  A)            explanation with a suitable schematic representation of the model.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            Software engineering has evolved through several programming paradigms-from early machine           (5)  
  programming to aspect-oriented and embedded client-server designs." Apply your understanding of  
  these design paradigms to illustrate, with suitable examples, how the shift from Control-Flow-Based  
  Design to Object-Oriented modularity and maintainability of complex embedded client-server  
  applications  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                 Explain the concept of cohesion in software design. Analyze and differentiate between temporal          (5)  
  cohesion and sequential cohesion with suitable examples to show how each impacts module  
  A)            design.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)            How would you identify and explain the level of coupling in a given software design? Is it true that in (5)  
  a good design, the modules should have low coupling? Why?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                 Design an Alumni-Student Mentorship Web Portal that facilitates mentorship, career guidance, and (5)  
  
  Page #1

networking between current students and alumni of an institution. The system should allow alumni  
  A)  
  to register, create and update their professional profiles, and specify areas of expertise or  
  mentorship interests. Students should be able to browse alumni profiles, send mentorship or career  
  advice requests, and schedule virtual or in-person mentorship sessions. The system should also  
  enable both alumni and students to communicate securely and track the status of mentorship  
  requests. Additionally, the portal should maintain records of sessions and allow administrators to  
  monitor overall engagement.  
  
  Using your understanding of UML Use Case Diagrams, apply the concepts to construct a use case  
  diagram for this application  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Consider a Health Monitoring System that tracks a patient's vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure,     (5)  
  oxygen level) through wearable sensors and sends alerts to doctors in case of abnormalities.  
  Apply your understanding of Use Case Modelling to identify the actors and major use cases, and  
  draw a schematic Component Diagram representing the system interactions.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                                                                                                                       (5)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Identify all linearly independent paths in the given program. Analyze how cyclomatic complexity can  
  be used as a metric to determine the number of linearly independent paths for any program, and  
  explain the steps involved in computing it.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)         Design a black-box test suite for a function that checks whether a character string (of up to twenty-    (5)  
  five characters in length) is a palindrome.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
